finding.claim: Broken authorization on /admin/drop: the result of Authorize(u, "dba") is discarded, so any authenticated user (any role, including none) can run DROP TABLE.
finding.source: Authenticated request to /admin/drop; user comes from request context via userFrom (api.go:22). Any role or empty Roles is accepted.
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27 (destructive, schema-level).

trace.note: Route /admin/drop registered to dropTable with no auth wrapper in this file.
dropTable entry point; attacker controls the request.
userFrom pulls *User from context; no role check yet.
Authorize(u, "dba") called; error return ignored, so execution always continues.
r.FormValue("t") concatenated into SQL and passed to runSQL; DROP executes.
runSQL sink (stub here; assumed to execute against the DB).

finding.guards_checked: Authorize at api.go:26 exists but its error is not checked (compare vacuum at api.go:33-36, which does check it). No middleware in this file enforces roles on /admin/drop. Whether authentication middleware sets the context user is not visible in this file.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize at api.go:26 is a bare statement, so its error return (defined at api.go:13-20) is discarded and execution always reaches the SQL at api.go:27. No role middleware is registered for /admin/drop at api.go:44. The only other guard is the allowlist-free concatenation at api.go:27, which provides no protection. Compare the checked call at api.go:33-36 in vacuum.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: Authorize's error is discarded at api.go:26, so any user returned by userFrom (api.go:25) reaches the unparameterized "DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27 via the route at api.go:44. The only caveat is that authentication that populates the context user is not visible in this file, and runSQL (api.go:41) is a stub, so the sink's execution is assumed rather than shown.

finding.claim: SQL injection in dropTable: the table name from the form is concatenated into SQL with no validation, quoting, or allowlist.
finding.source: r.FormValue("t") (query string or form body), api.go:27.
finding.sink: runSQL(...) at api.go:27 (raw SQL string concatenation).

trace.note: t is concatenated into the DROP TABLE statement without validation.

finding.guards_checked: No validation, identifier quoting, or allowlist on t. Injection beyond the DROP depends on whether the driver permits multiple statements, which this file does not show. Exploitation needs a caller who passes the authorization bug in F1 or a legitimately authorized dba.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is the only candidate control, but its error return is discarded at api.go:26 as a bare statement, so the "dba" check never blocks the request. No parameterization, identifier quoting, or table allowlist exists between r.FormValue("t") (api.go:27) and runSQL (api.go:41, a stub that does nothing here). Unlike vacuum (api.go:33-35), dropTable has no error check. The only other gate, userFrom (api.go:22), is a type assertion that panics without a user in context, and no auth middleware appears in this file.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: api.go:27 concatenates the request value into "DROP TABLE " with no guard, and the Authorize result is discarded at api.go:26, so any user who reaches /admin/drop (api.go:44) can inject into the statement. The attacker is a low-privilege authenticated user, not one who already holds dba, so the finding holds. Driver multi-statement support only affects how far the injection goes; arbitrary table drop by name is already exploitable.

finding.claim: Destructive admin action is state-changing and not restricted to POST, and FormValue also reads the query string. A cross-site request (for example an or link) from a logged-in browser could trigger DROP TABLE if auth is cookie-based.
finding.source: Cross-site GET or POST with ?t=... sent by the victim's browser.

trace.note: HandleFunc registers /admin/drop for all HTTP methods.
FormValue reads ?t= from the query string, so a GET request works.

finding.guards_checked: No method check, CSRF token, or Origin/Referer check in this file. Exploitability depends on how authentication is carried (cookie vs. header). Not visible here.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 is the only control. It returns an error, but the call is a bare statement and the result is discarded, so it does not block anything. The vacuum handler at api.go:33-35 checks the result correctly, which makes the drop handler's omission clear. runSQL at api.go:27 receives unparameterized concatenation of r.FormValue("t") with no allowlist. No method check, CSRF token, or Origin/Referer check exists in this file.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: api.go:44 registers /admin/drop for all methods and api.go:27 reads ?t= via FormValue. The dba role check at api.go:26 discards its error, so any request whose context carries a user (userFrom at api.go:22-25) reaches runSQL("DROP TABLE " + t) at api.go:27, which is a SQL injection and an authorization bypass. The cross-site (CSRF) vector the candidate describes depends on cookie-based auth set by middleware that is not in this directory, so that specific precondition remains unverified, but the discarded authorization check is confirmed regardless of the attack vector.

finding.claim: Unchecked type assertion in userFrom panics when no *User is in the request context, which can crash the handler on any unauthenticated request to /admin/*.
finding.source: Unauthenticated request to /admin/drop or /admin/vacuum where no user was placed in context.

trace.note: Route reaches dropTable or vacuum without auth middleware in this file.
dropTable calls userFrom; api.go:32 does the same in vacuum.
Value("user") returns nil; assertion panics. net/http recovers per-request, so the impact is a logged panic, not a process crash.

finding.guards_checked: No nil or ok-form check on the assertion. The string key "user" is untyped, so it is collision-prone. Impact is limited to per-request panics, and the request still does not succeed, so this is not an auth bypass.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only Go file in the directory is api.go, so no middleware wraps the routes registered at api.go:44-45. The assertion at api.go:22 has no nil or ok-form check, and nothing between the request and the assertion recovers from or prevents the panic. The Authorize calls (api.go:26, api.go:33) run after userFrom has already panicked, so they are not a guard here.
verdict.reason: An anonymous request to /admin/drop or /admin/vacuum reaches userFrom (api.go:25, api.go:32), where Value("user") returns nil and the assertion at api.go:22 panics; this is a per-request panic that net/http recovers, so the impact is a failed request plus a logged panic, not a process crash or an auth bypass, which makes the claim's severity overstated even though the trace is accurate.
